title: AI tools for Forward Deployed Engineering — Vasuman Moza, Varick Agents
talk_summary: Varick Agents argues the next bottleneck is understanding and redesigning business processes around AI, not raw model execution. They build an AI forward-deployed-engineer stack: a dependency-graph source of truth, embedded workflow assistant, custom graph-traversal tools, post-trained concise models, and eventually autonomous small workflow changes.

takeaways.technique: Dependency graph as work source of truth
takeaways.what_they_do: They represent company processes as a dependency graph rather than free text, making owners, blockers, cycles, and redundancy explicit.
An assistant embedded in the workflow builder watches the FDE construct a process and prompts for missed edge cases and process ownership before deployment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you forgot about this edge case

takeaways.technique: Custom graph-traversal tools for aliases and DAG checks
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose custom tools for traversing the knowledge graph, including resolving aliases like multiple Mikes and detecting redundancy or cycles.
takeaways.evidence_quote: make sure person A and person B are actually the same person

takeaways.technique: Offline eval/RL environment for context retrieval
takeaways.what_they_do: They create an RL environment with custom graph tools to train reliable traversal and context extraction, not just prompt a frontier model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we create an RL environment where we have exposed our own custom tools

takeaways.technique: Post-train small open model for concise analysis
takeaways.what_they_do: They post-train open-source models to produce concise, prioritized process analysis because frontier models are verbose and miss what clients care about.
They plan an autonomous assistant that reads client change requests, queries company understanding, and ships small workflow changes without FDE involvement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ship an autonomous change to the workflow
